habitat: Flocks fly in compact groups in thornveld, riverine forest and suburbia, favouring the moister regions.
summary: A common resident, identified by the red mask. The rump and underparts are grey-white, the eye is blue, the bill is black and the legs are red. The call is a descending tree-ree-ree, often repeated, in flight and at rest.

similar.note: Speckled Mousebird is dull brown, with a black mask and a black-and-white bill, not a red mask.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^14=16384 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 8192–32768.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

viewNotes.note: Red mask and a long tail, in a compact flock.
Red mask, blue eye and black bill.
Flocks fly in compact groups. The upperwing was not named.

calls.description: A descending tree-ree-ree, frequently repeated, in flight and at rest. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Grahamstown, Eastern Cape. The filename is Red-faced Mousebirds.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common resident. The family text on the page says immatures are duller, and that was not stored as a separate plumage because it is not specific to this species. Population figures were left unchanged.
